papers.title: Keelman's verse
lines: Weigh, hey, the keel row. Written out in a careful hand for a child who could not yet read.
In the margin: 'Sing it to your lass, even if you cannot sing. Especially if you cannot sing.'

papers.title: Season ticket stub
lines: Gallowgate End. Saturday, three o'clock. Third generation of us.
Dad said: 'Never leave before the whistle.' We have not, in fact, left before it in forty years.

papers.title: Vindolanda-style note
lines: A copy of a wooden writing tablet from Vindolanda: a parcel for a soldier on the Wall.
Socks, sandals and two pairs of underpants. The museum card notes that nobody has improved on this in nineteen centuries.

papers.title: Pony's retirement card
lines: After eleven years underground, Blackie is to be brought to grass.
The pit lads lined up to see him blink in the sun. Nobody was crying. It was the dust.

trail.clue: A pit pony is buried under a stone near the lamp post. The lads left a tin of coins at his feet.

papers.title: Hiker's postcard
lines: Walked the whole wall in a week. Fell in a bog on day two, got over it by day three.
The sheep have opinions. The views have opinions too, and they are better ones.
